description: Given a Prefect flow with an input-driven branch, a runtime output-driven branch, or an allow_failure pattern, author the matching Orchestra YAML — mutually-exclusive condition: stages for branches, an upstream set_outputs: true task feeding a runtime OUTPUTS condition, and treat_failure_as_warning for allow_failure, never conflating the three.

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra (see files/config_load_mode_branch.py). The `full_refresh` flow parameter decides at trigger time whether the backfill branch or the incremental branch runs — only one of the two tasks actually executes per run. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline with a full_refresh boolean input, a stage conditioned on ${{ inputs.full_refresh == true }} running run_backfill, and a mutually-exclusive stage conditioned on the false case running run_incremental.

assertions.text: Pipeline declares an input for the branch decision
full_refresh is referenced both as an input and inside a condition expression
A condition references inputs.full_refresh (a trigger-time / parameter-driven branch, not a runtime OUTPUTS lookup)
Both branch stages carry a condition key
The two conditions are genuinely mutually exclusive (one tests full_refresh true, the other tests false/not-true) rather than both able to evaluate true, or both false, in the same run

run_backfill and run_incremental land as separate tasks under their respective conditioned stages, not merged into a single task with if/else routing logic ported over verbatim from the Prefect flow body

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra (see files/runtime_row_count_branch.py). Whether orders get loaded or a no-data notice fires depends on a row count computed during the run via `.submit()`/`.result()`, not on any parameter passed in at trigger time. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline where check_staging_orders becomes an upstream task with set_outputs: true, and two downstream stages condition on that task's OUTPUTS — one for the positive/has-rows case running load_orders, one for the complementary case running send_no_data_notice.

assertions.text: The upstream check is a task that sets outputs for downstream conditions to read
A condition references the upstream task's OUTPUTS via ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS
Downstream stages are sequenced after the check via depends_on
The value surfaced by check_staging_orders (the row count) is a real value from the source logic (e.g. row_count), not an invented placeholder key unrelated to what the task actually returns

load_orders conditions on the positive/has-rows case and send_no_data_notice conditions on the true complementary case, correctly mirroring new_row_count > 0 vs the zero case rather than both being gated on the same condition or one left unconditioned

evals.prompt: Convert this Prefect flow to Orchestra (see files/allow_failure_cleanup.py). purge_temp_tables is best-effort cleanup — the `allow_failure` wrapping around it means load_orders must proceed regardless of whether cleanup succeeded, and a failure alert should only fire if the load itself comes back with zero rows. Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: An Orchestra pipeline where purge_temp_tables carries treat_failure_as_warning: true so its failure doesn't hard-fail the run, load_orders is sequenced after it via depends_on without being gated behind a success condition on the cleanup task, load_orders sets outputs, and a downstream stage conditions send_load_failure_alert on load_orders' OUTPUTS equalling zero.

assertions.text: purge_temp_tables (or its converted task) carries treat_failure_as_warning: true so allow_failure semantics are preserved
At least one task has treat_failure_as_warning set to true
load_orders sets outputs so the downstream zero-rows check can read them
A condition references load_orders' OUTPUTS via ORCHESTRA.PIPELINE_RUN_TASKS
Task groups are chained via depends_on (load stage runs after cleanup, alert stage runs after load)

load_orders is sequenced after purge_temp_tables via depends_on but is not itself gated behind a condition on cleanup's success — allow_failure means downstream continues regardless of the upstream outcome, it is not modeled as a branch condition

treat_failure_as_warning is applied to purge_temp_tables (the task that may legitimately fail), not mistakenly attached to load_orders or send_load_failure_alert, and the alert's condition checks the zero-rows case specifically rather than an always-true/always-false stand-in
